classes.pure: A function of its arguments only. Allowed everywhere.
classes.context: Reads the caller's context: the user, the clock, the document's state and id. Not allowed in auto formulas.
classes.lookup: Reads one value from a table or stack. In auto formulas only against explicit tables.
classes.query: Reads rows from a table or stack. Not allowed in auto formulas.
classes.secret: Reads a secret the host program supplies for a connection. Allowed only in the request of an action definition.

functions.name: IF
functions.summary: The second argument when the condition is TRUE, else the third. Only the chosen branch is evaluated. IF c THEN a ELSE b is the same expression.

functions.name: AND
functions.summary: TRUE when every condition is TRUE, evaluated left to right and stopping at the first FALSE. Also the operator a AND b.

functions.name: OR
functions.summary: TRUE when any condition is TRUE, evaluated left to right and stopping at the first TRUE. Also the operator a OR b.

functions.name: NOT
functions.summary: The opposite of the condition. Also the operator NOT a.

functions.name: ISBLANK
functions.summary: TRUE only for a blank, never for a stored 0 or an empty text.

functions.name: ISNOTBLANK
functions.summary: TRUE for anything but a blank.

functions.name: IFERROR
functions.summary: The value, or the fallback when evaluating the value stops with an error. The fallback must have the value's type or be blank.

functions.name: ROUND
functions.summary: Rounds to the given decimal places by the method: half_up (the default, a half away from zero), half_even, down (toward zero), up (away from zero), floor or ceiling, written in the formula. Negative digits round to tens, hundreds and so on. On an exact value the digits are written in the formula and give the result's scale; the result keeps the kind, decimal or money.

functions.name: FLOOR
functions.summary: Rounds down, toward minus infinity, at the given decimal places. On an exact value the digits give the result's scale.

functions.name: CEILING
functions.summary: Rounds up, toward plus infinity, at the given decimal places. On an exact value the digits give the result's scale.

functions.name: TRUNC
functions.summary: Cuts the number toward zero at the given decimal places. On an exact value the digits give the result's scale.

functions.name: ABS
functions.summary: The magnitude of the number. An exact value keeps its kind and scale.

functions.name: SIGN
functions.summary: -1, 0 or 1 by the sign of the number; an int for an exact value.

functions.name: MIN
functions.summary: The smallest of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Blank when nothing is left. The values are of one family: all numbers, or all exact, at the largest scale, money of one currency. In a live variable MIN(invoices.net) is the smallest value of a column of a list of the document (ADR-0081).

functions.name: MAX
functions.summary: The largest of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Blank when nothing is left. The values are of one family, as for MIN. In a live variable MAX(invoices.net) is the largest value of a column of a list of the document (ADR-0081).

functions.name: SUM
functions.summary: The sum of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Exact values add exactly at the largest scale, money of one currency. In a live variable SUM(invoices.net) is the sum of a column of a list of the document, over the rows its reader may read (ADR-0081). Over the lines the document itself holds it stands in any formula, and its argument may be an expression of their columns: SUM(lines.qty * lines.price).

functions.name: AVERAGE
functions.summary: The mean of the numbers and array elements given, blanks skipped. Blank when nothing is left. Exact values divide at the largest scale plus four, half away from zero. In a live variable AVERAGE(invoices.net) is the mean of a column of a list of the document, and in the column position of a LOOKUP the mean over the matching rows (ADR-0081).

functions.name: COUNT
functions.summary: How many of the values and array elements given are not blank. COUNT of a rows value is its number of rows. In a live variable COUNT(invoices) is the number of rows of a list of the document, and COUNT(invoices.net) how many of them have a value in the column (ADR-0081). Over a list the document itself holds, its lines or its tags, it stands in any formula: COUNT(lines).

functions.name: POWER
functions.summary: The number raised to the power. The same as the ^ operator.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.summary: The square root. A negative number is the error not_a_number.

functions.name: EXP
functions.summary: e raised to the number.

functions.name: LN
functions.summary: The natural logarithm. Zero or a negative number is the error not_a_number.

functions.name: LOG
functions.summary: The logarithm in the given base, 10 when omitted. A number at or below zero, or a base at or below zero or equal to 1, is the error not_a_number.

functions.name: MOD
functions.summary: The remainder, with the sign of the divisor as in Excel. A zero divisor is the error div_by_zero. Exact values give an exact remainder at the larger scale.

functions.name: DECIMAL
functions.summary: The value as an exact decimal with the given places, written in the formula, rounded by the method as ROUND does, half_up when omitted. A number is rounded at the places; a decimal or money is rescaled, money losing its currency. Blank stays blank.

functions.name: NUMBER
functions.summary: The nearest number to an exact value, for the functions that need a number such as POWER and SQRT. Blank stays blank.

functions.name: MONEY
functions.summary: The amount as money in the currency, three upper-case letters such as "PLN"; anything else is the error bad_text. A number literal amount is read exactly. A blank amount is blank.

functions.name: MONEYVALUE
functions.summary: The money written as an amount, a space and a currency, such as "12.30 PLN", at the given places, written in the formula. Empty text is blank; a malformed text is the error bad_text; an amount with more places than asked is the error inexact.

functions.name: DECIMALVALUE
functions.summary: The exact number written in the text, at the given places, written in the formula. Empty text is blank; a malformed text is the error bad_text; more places than asked is the error inexact; more than 18 digits is the error overflow.

functions.name: AMOUNT
functions.summary: The amount of a money as a decimal at the same scale. Blank for a blank money.

functions.name: CURRENCY
functions.summary: The currency code of a money. Blank for a blank money.

functions.name: DATE
functions.summary: The calendar day given. Fractions are truncated and overflow carries: month 14 is February of the next year, day 0 is the last day of the month before.

functions.name: DATEVALUE
functions.summary: The calendar day written as YYYY-MM-DD. Empty text is blank; anything else, a time of day included, is the error bad_text.

functions.name: DATETIMEVALUE
functions.summary: The instant written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DD, read as UTC. Empty text is blank; anything else is the error bad_text.

functions.name: DATEOF
functions.summary: The calendar day of an instant, in UTC. Blank for a blank datetime.

functions.name: DATETIME
functions.summary: Midnight UTC of a calendar day. Blank for a blank date.

functions.name: YEAR
functions.summary: The year of the date or instant. Blank for a blank.

functions.name: MONTH
functions.summary: The month of the date or instant, 1 to 12. Blank for a blank.

functions.name: DAY
functions.summary: The day of the month of the date or instant. Blank for a blank.

functions.name: QUARTER
functions.summary: The quarter of the date or instant, 1 to 4. Blank for a blank.

functions.name: DAYS
functions.summary: Calendar days from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, an instant taken at its UTC midnight first. Blank when either is blank.

functions.name: DAYSBETWEEN
functions.summary: Calendar day boundaries crossed from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, negative when the end comes first. Blank when either is blank.

functions.name: MONTHSBETWEEN
functions.summary: Calendar month boundaries crossed from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, negative when the end comes first. Blank when either is blank.

functions.name: YEARSBETWEEN
functions.summary: Calendar year boundaries crossed from the start to the end, both dates or both datetimes, negative when the end comes first. Blank when either is blank.

functions.name: ADDDAYS
functions.summary: The date or instant moved by the given number of days: whole days on a date, fractions moving the time of day on a datetime. Blank for a blank.

functions.name: ADDMONTHS
functions.summary: The date or instant moved by whole months, keeping the day of month and the time of day and clamping to the last day of a shorter month. Blank for a blank.

functions.name: ADDYEARS
functions.summary: The date or instant moved by whole years, clamping 29 February to 28 February in a common year. Blank for a blank.

functions.name: NOW
functions.summary: The current instant in UTC, to the second.

functions.name: TODAY
functions.summary: The current calendar day in UTC.

functions.name: USER
functions.summary: The id of the user on whose behalf the formula runs. Blank for a system recompute.

functions.name: INGROUP
functions.summary: TRUE when the current user is a member of the named group.

functions.name: INROLE
functions.summary: TRUE when the current user holds the named role of the app the formula belongs to: INROLE("approver"). The app names its roles; each server says which groups and people hold them. The role is written as text, never worked out, and the app must name it.

functions.name: USERKIND
functions.summary: What the current user is: person, agent or service. Blank when the host program does not say.

functions.name: ACTINGFOR
functions.summary: The id of whoever the current user acts for. Blank when it acts for itself.

functions.name: STATE
functions.summary: The state of the document the formula runs over. Blank for a class without states.

functions.name: ID
functions.summary: The id of the document the formula runs over. Blank when there is no document.

functions.name: REF
functions.summary: A pointer to a document, which a ref compares with. With no argument it is the pointer to the document the formula belongs to, order = REF(), and stands where ID() may; in the condition of a QUERY it is the document the list belongs to. With a class, written as a text, and an id it is the pointer to that document, REF("Order", "ORD-17"), and stands anywhere; blank when the id is blank.

functions.name: CREATEDAT
functions.summary: The instant the document the formula runs over was created. Blank when there is no document.

functions.name: CREATEDBY
functions.summary: The id of the user whose command created the document. Blank when the command named nobody.

functions.name: UPDATEDAT
functions.summary: The instant the current version of the document was made.

functions.name: UPDATEDBY
functions.summary: The id of the user whose command made the current version of the document. Blank when the command named nobody.

functions.name: ENTEREDAT
functions.summary: The instant the document entered the state it is in. A transition back into the same state is an entry too. Blank for a class without states.

functions.name: ENTEREDBY
functions.summary: The id of the user whose command moved the document into the state it is in. Blank when the command named nobody.

functions.name: ENTEREDFROM
functions.summary: The state the document was in before the one it is in: that same state after a transition back into it, blank while it is in the state it was created in.

functions.name: VERSION
functions.summary: The version of the document the formula runs over. Blank when there is no document.

functions.name: FIRSTENTERED
functions.summary: The instant the document first entered the state. Blank when it never did.

functions.name: FIRSTENTEREDBY
functions.summary: The id of the user whose command first moved the document into the state. Blank when it never entered it, and when the command named nobody.

functions.name: LASTENTERED
functions.summary: The instant the document last entered the state, a transition back into it counted. Blank when it never did.

functions.name: LASTENTEREDBY
functions.summary: The id of the user whose command last moved the document into the state. Blank when it never entered it, and when the command named nobody.

functions.name: FIRSTLEFT
functions.summary: The instant the document first left the state. Blank when it never left it.

functions.name: FIRSTLEFTBY
functions.summary: The id of the user whose command first moved the document out of the state. Blank when it never left it, and when the command named nobody.

functions.name: LASTLEFT
functions.summary: The instant the document last left the state; for a document that is in the state, the time before. Blank when it never left it.

functions.name: LASTLEFTBY
functions.summary: The id of the user whose command last moved the document out of the state. Blank when it never left it, and when the command named nobody.

functions.name: ENTRIES
functions.summary: How many times the document entered the state, a transition back into it counted. 0 when it never did, blank when there is no document.

functions.name: DAYSIN
functions.summary: The days the document has spent in the state in all, with fractions, up to now when it is there. 0 when it never was, blank when there is no document.

functions.name: FIRSTEDITOR
functions.summary: The id of the first user who created the document in the state or changed it there. Moving it in or out is not a change. Blank when nobody did.

functions.name: LASTEDITOR
functions.summary: The id of the last user who created the document in the state or changed it there. Moving it in or out is not a change. Blank when nobody did.

functions.name: LEFT
functions.summary: The first count characters, the whole text when the count is longer. A negative count is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: RIGHT
functions.summary: The last count characters, the whole text when the count is longer. A negative count is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: MID
functions.summary: The characters from the 1-based position, to the end when the length is omitted or runs past it. A position below 1 or a negative length is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: LEN
functions.summary: The number of characters, counted as Unicode code points.

functions.name: TRIM
functions.summary: The text without leading and trailing spaces and with runs of inner spaces collapsed to one, as in Excel.

functions.name: UPPER
functions.summary: The text in upper case, Unicode simple case mapping.

functions.name: LOWER
functions.summary: The text in lower case, Unicode simple case mapping.

functions.name: PROPER
functions.summary: The first letter of every word in upper case and the rest in lower case.

functions.name: URLENCODE
functions.summary: The text made safe for a URL: letters, digits and - . _ ~ stay, and every other character becomes its UTF-8 bytes as %XX with upper-case hex digits, so a space is %20. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: REPLACE
functions.summary: The text with length characters from the 1-based position replaced by the new text. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: SUBSTITUTE
functions.summary: The text with every occurrence of the old text replaced by the new text. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: CONCAT
functions.summary: The arguments joined into one text, each rendered as TEXT does. The same as the & operator. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: REPEAT
functions.summary: The text repeated count times. A negative count, or a result longer than the text limit, is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: FINDFIRST
functions.summary: The 1-based position of the first occurrence of the search text, case-sensitive, or 0 when absent.

functions.name: FINDLAST
functions.summary: The 1-based position of the last occurrence of the search text, case-sensitive, or 0 when absent.

functions.name: PAD
functions.summary: The text padded on the left with the fill character, a space when omitted, up to the width. Longer text is returned unchanged. A width above the text limit is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: REGEXREPLACE
functions.summary: The text with every match of the RE2 pattern replaced by the replacement, taken literally: no backreferences. An invalid pattern is rejected at definition time when it is a literal; an invalid pattern built at run time is the error bad_text. A result longer than the text limit is the error out_of_range.

functions.name: TEXT
functions.summary: The value as text: numbers with 15 significant digits and no trailing zeros, exact values with every digit of their scale, money as the amount, a space and the currency, dates as YYYY-MM-DD, datetimes as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, TRUE and FALSE, refs as Class:id, blank as empty text.

functions.name: VALUE
functions.summary: The number written in the text: optional sign, digits, fraction and exponent, with a dot as the decimal point. Empty text is blank; anything else is the error bad_text.

functions.name: INDEX
functions.summary: The value at the 1-based position of a column of a list of the document, in the order of the list: INDEX(lines.what, 2). A position that is no whole number, or that the list does not have, is the error out_of_range. The list is one the document holds, its lines or its tags, INDEX(tags, 1), or in a live variable a list that is a QUERY (ADR-0081).

functions.name: FILTER
functions.summary: The rows of a list of the document that meet the condition, for a function over a list to work on: SUM(FILTER(lines, delivered).price), JOIN(FILTER(lines, NOT delivered).what, ", "). Inside the condition a bare name is a column of the row and THIS.name a variable of the document, as in COUNTIF. It gives a list, and a list stands only inside a function over a list (ADR-0081).

functions.name: SORT
functions.summary: A list of the document in another order, for a function that goes by the order: FIRST(SORT(lines, {-price}).what) is the dearest line. The columns stand in braces, a minus before one for descending; rows the columns order alike keep the order of the list, and a blank comes before every value. The rules are those of FILTER.

functions.name: TOP
functions.summary: The first rows of a list of the document, as many as the count says: SUM(TOP(SORT(lines, {-price}), 3).price) adds up the three dearest lines. The count is a value of the document; a blank one is 0, and one that is below 0 or no whole number is the error out_of_range. The rules are those of FILTER.

functions.name: UNIQUE
functions.summary: The different values of a column of a list of the document, blanks skipped, each where it first stands: JOIN(UNIQUE(lines.what), ", "). It gives a list of single values, for JOIN, FIRST, LAST, INDEX, COUNT and CONTAINS to work on. The rules are those of FILTER.

functions.name: FIRST
functions.summary: The value of a column in the first row of a list of the document, in the order of the list: FIRST(lines.what). Blank for a list with no rows. The list is one the document holds, its lines or its tags, or in a live variable a list that is a QUERY (ADR-0081).

functions.name: LAST
functions.summary: The value of a column in the last row of a list of the document: LAST(lines.what). Blank for a list with no rows. The rules are those of FIRST.

functions.name: CONTAINS
functions.summary: TRUE when some row of a list of the document has the value in the column, compared as the = operator does: CONTAINS(tags, "urgent"), CONTAINS(lines.what, "ink"). FALSE for a list with no rows. The value is a value of the document, the same for every row. The rules are those of FIRST.

functions.name: JOIN
functions.summary: The values of a column of a list of the document as one text, in the order of the list, each written as TEXT writes it, blanks skipped, the separator between them: JOIN(lines.what, ", "). Blank when nothing is left; a text past the limit of a text is the error out_of_range. The rules are those of FIRST.

functions.name: JSONVALUE
functions.summary: One value read from a json value at a dotted path such as address.city or items.0.sku, as text: numbers as TEXT renders them, booleans as TRUE and FALSE. Blank when the path is absent or null; an object or array at the path is the error bad_text. Convert with VALUE or DATEVALUE.

functions.name: SECRET
functions.summary: The secret of that name, which the connection of an action definition declares and the host program supplies when the request is sent. The name is a text literal. Only the request of an action definition may use it; the engine stores no secret.

functions.name: LOOKUP
functions.summary: One column of the first row of the source, in key order, that matches the condition; blank when none does. In place of the column, COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX, AVERAGE, MEDIAN or COUNTUNIQUE over one expression of the source's columns answers for every matching row. Inside, bare names are the source's columns and THIS.name reaches the document.

functions.name: QUERY
functions.summary: The documents of the source, a class, or the rows of the source, a table, that match the condition, with the given columns, in the given sort; every one when there is no condition. Several columns are written in braces, {number, net}, and so are several to sort by, a leading - for descending. It is the whole formula of a live variable, read for the reader, who gets the documents and the values they may read; or of a triggered variable of type rows, which keeps the list with the document, one list for everybody. A column may be a total over a variable of a class, COUNT(id), SUM(net), MIN, MAX, AVERAGE or COUNTUNIQUE: the plain columns then say what the lines are grouped by, one line for each group, and the list may be sorted by a total, {-SUM(net)}; such a list is read live. Not built yet: the groupby and limit arguments, which nothing needs to write, and a QUERY anywhere else.

functions.name: COUNTIF
functions.summary: How many rows of a list of the document meet the condition: COUNTIF(invoices, state = "paid"). A list is a live variable whose formula is a QUERY, and the function stands in a live variable. Inside the condition a bare name is a column of the listed class and THIS.name a variable of the document. It is one question to the listed class, asked for whoever reads the variable: only the rows they may read are counted (ADR-0081). A list is also what the document itself holds, its lines or its tags: COUNTIF(lines, qty > 1). There the function stands in any formula, the rows are the document's own and the same for every reader, and an element of an array is called value.

functions.name: SUMIF
functions.summary: The sum of a column over the rows of a list that meet the condition: SUMIF(invoices, state <> "paid", net). The rules are those of COUNTIF and of SUM: blanks skipped, exact values added exactly, money of one currency.

functions.name: MINIF
functions.summary: The smallest value of a column over the rows of a list that meet the condition; blank when none does. The rules are those of COUNTIF and of MIN.

functions.name: MAXIF
functions.summary: The largest value of a column over the rows of a list that meet the condition; blank when none does. The rules are those of COUNTIF and of MAX.

functions.name: AVERAGEIF
functions.summary: The mean of a column over the rows of a list that meet the condition; blank when none does. The rules are those of COUNTIF and of AVERAGE.

functions.name: MEDIAN
functions.summary: The middle value of a column of rows, blanks skipped; of an even number of values the mean of the two in the middle; blank when nothing is left. Exact values give an exact answer at one place more, money in one currency. It works over rows alone: in a live variable over a list of the document, MEDIAN(invoices.net), over the lines the document itself holds, MEDIAN(lines.price), and in the column position of a LOOKUP (ADR-0081).

functions.name: COUNTUNIQUE
functions.summary: How many different values a column of rows has, blanks skipped, compared as = compares them; money of two currencies is two values. It works over rows alone: in a live variable over a list of the document, COUNTUNIQUE(invoices.state), over the lines or the tags the document itself holds, COUNTUNIQUE(tags), and in the column position of a LOOKUP (ADR-0081).

functions.name: ANY
functions.summary: TRUE when some row of a list meets the condition: ANY(invoices, state = "draft"). FALSE for a list with no rows. The rules are those of COUNTIF.

functions.name: ALL
functions.summary: TRUE when every row of a list meets the condition: ALL(invoices, state = "paid"). A row on which the condition is blank does not meet it; TRUE for a list with no rows. The rules are those of COUNTIF.
